references.text: Isaiah prophesies about one who cries out in the wilderness to prepare the way for the Lord, pointing forward to John the Baptist's role.
Malachi predicts Elijah who will come before the great and dreadful day of the Lord, which is associated with the coming of John the Baptist.
Jesus identifies John as 'the Elijah who was to come,' directly linking John to the prophecies in the Old Testament.
Mark introduces John the Baptist and his role in preparing the people for the Lord's coming, parallel to Luke's description.
John the Baptist denies being the Christ and refers to himself as 'a voice crying out in the wilderness,' in line with Isaiah's prophecy.
